findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the live disposable ticket must be resolvable in the tickets store CI reads (the GitHub `tickets` branch) — i.e. published/replicated there before the change is pushed — or reuse an already-published ticket, so the CI require-ticket gate can pass and cast Verified+1.
evidence: .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:99-124 mounts the GitHub `tickets` branch as REBAR_TRACKER_DIR and runs `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD`; a well-formed trailer that does NOT resolve in that store fails the require-ticket job -> Verified-1
Sibling infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh:83-89 uses a REAL committed ticket (leafy-vogue-ingot) exactly because CI's 'require resolvable rebar ticket' job fails otherwise
gerrit-verify.yaml:73 'every commit to main must reference a rebar ticket that RESOLVES in the store'
findings.finding: The live PASS path can never earn Verified+1 unless the disposable rebar-ticket is resolvable in the GitHub `tickets` store that CI's ticket gate reads; the plan specifies a 'resolvable full-canonical trailer' and a 'live disposable ticket' but not that the ticket must be published to the tickets branch before CI runs.
scenarios: Operator runs the live E2E with a freshly-minted disposable ticket that exists only locally / not on the GitHub tickets branch: CI ticket-gate fails, Verified goes -1, the two-vote wait can never pass, and the harness cannot reach submit/replication assertions.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the live path either reuses an existing published ticket or creates the disposable ticket AND replicates it to the GitHub `tickets` branch (mirroring how gerrit-verify.yaml mounts REBAR_TRACKER_DIR from that branch) before pushing the change, so `rebar verify-commit-ticket` resolves it and CI casts Verified+1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency/ownership contract for `feature/e2e-gate-smoke` and the live disposable ticket: either use a per-run unique suffix/ref (and clean up only that run's ref) or document that the live E2E is single-flight and must not run concurrently.
evidence: 'The script must create/update the temporary feature branch for the run ... clean it up after the run by deleting the temporary feature/e2e-gate-smoke branch/ref'
Fixed branch name `feature/e2e-gate-smoke` implies no per-run uniqueness; create-then-use-then-delete on a shared name is a TOCTOU/ownership gap under concurrent runs.
findings.finding: The temporary feature branch `feature/e2e-gate-smoke` and the live disposable ticket are fixed-named shared resources whose ownership/concurrency the plan does not address; two concurrent or overlapping E2E runs would collide on the same ref/ticket (check-then-act create on a fixed name), and one run's cleanup could delete the branch another run is mid-exercise on.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the branch/ticket a per-run unique suffix (e.g. run id / timestamp) so create/observe/delete operate on a run-owned ref, and have cleanup target only that suffixed ref.
